chapter.title: ECS, EKS, Fargate and ECR
chapter.notes: Frequency note (third-party research from _build/spec/FREQUENCY.md; planning input only, never evidence). Containers (ECS, EKS, Fargate, ECR) are rank 5 of 42: 5 first-hand reports, and one says 'more than expected'; strong. Reported sub-topics: Fargate vs EC2 launch type, task roles, ECS Anywhere and EKS Anywhere, EKS Cluster Autoscaler and Metrics Server, Karpenter, migrating applications to containers. FREQUENCY suggests more depth than a typical medium chapter, mainly for EKS scaling. Pairs to decide: ECS vs EKS (existing Kubernetes, portability, EKS Anywhere vs the simplest AWS-native choice); Fargate vs Lambda; Fargate vs EC2 capacity. Stem signals: 'LEAST operational overhead' (Fargate), 'existing Kubernetes', 'minimal code changes'. Registry notes: ECS Anywhere, EKS Anywhere and EKS Distro are recognition-only service cards (cards list). EKS Anywhere and EKS Distro have no guide on an allowed host, so use their product and FAQ pages and the EKS deployment options page. What's New has no tag for the two Anywhere products; their items carry amazon-ecs and amazon-eks. AWS App Runner appears in the decision guides and in the Containers on AWS whitepaper, but it is not in the in-scope list and it is on the Services in Maintenance page: do not teach it as an answer. App2Container is the AWS tool behind bullet 2.1.K8; it is not an in-scope entry.
